title: Feature Activation Lifecycle Timeline
content:
Purpose:
A compact operational timeline and KPI sheet for the staged activation of the new per-route traffic shaping feature. This doc is intentionally tactical — meant for product-ops, SRE, release engineering, and the launch engineers running the first two canaries.

Executive summary (one line):
Roll traffic to 10% -> 30% -> 60% over three days with automated rollback triggers; track latency P95, error rate, and token-cost delta per 1M tokens.

High-level milestones (rough dates; adjust per sprint):
1) Feature freeze + QA sign-off (D0) â€” 2025-01-20
2) Internal dogfood + perf run (D1) â€” 2025-01-22 to 2025-01-24
3) Canary A (small customer cohort, 5 instances) rollout start (D3) â€” 2025-01-27
4) Canary B (broader internal + trusted customers) rollout start (D6) â€” 2025-01-30
5) Ramp to 30% traffic (D8) â€” 2025-02-01
6) Ramp to 60% traffic (D10) â€” 2025-02-03
7) Full availability and deprecation of old route (D14) â€” 2025-02-07

KPI tracker (snapshot control panel):
- Latency (P95) target: <= 120ms for hosted API, <= 140ms for dedicated pools
- Error rate (5xx) target: < 0.1% sustained; immediate action at >0.5%
- Token cost delta: target <= +6% at 95th percentile; investigate if > +10%
- Throughput: maintain baseline of 1500 reqs/min per pool for dedicated clusters
- Quality regressions: BLEU/ROUGE-style automated eval set pass rate >= 98% (see eval harness link)
- Adoption signals: first-week active routes >= 12 (internal/customer), stickiness measured by repeat calls/day

Per-milestone readiness checklist (yes/no + owner):
- D0: QA sign-off (owner: Sofia Ramirez) â€” test matrix completed; known failures triaged; go/no-go decided
- D1: Perf run (owner: Liam Chen) â€” baseline perf artifacts uploaded to S3; e2e load test playbook executed
- D3: Canary A deploy (owner: Oliver Grant) â€” rollback automation compiled and tested; incident playbook linked
- D6: Canary B deploy (owner: Maya Patel) â€” customer communication sent; telemetry dashboards live
- D8: 30% ramp (owner: Release Eng oncall) â€” autoscaling target verified; cost alerts enabled
- D10: 60% ramp (owner: Eng SRE) â€” regional capacity confirmed; fallbacks validated
- D14: GA (owner: Product Ops lead) â€” docs updated; migration path created for customers on legacy route

Runbook snippets (quick triggers):
- Immediate rollback: if P95 increases >50% for 5 consecutive minutes OR 5xx >0.5% for 3 minutes -> switch traffic to previous variant and page Eng SRE
- Traffic throttle: if token-cost delta exceeds threshold and adoption is low, pause further ramps and open cost-insight ticket
- Partial fallback: if regional capacity shortage in eu-west-1, route 25% of eu traffic to eu-north-1 until capacity replenished

Risk register (top 6):
1) Increased token cost causing negative unit economics for a major customer â€” mitigations: precompute caching settings; enable quantized model fallback; set cost alerting
2) Latency spike under specific prompt patterns â€” mitigations: add prompt-based prefix caching; extend KV cache TTL for long-horizon prompts
3) Incomplete telemetry for dedicated customers â€” mitigations: instrument tenant-level metrics; ensure token breakdown logs are surfaced to console
4) Rollout procedure gaps between release and SRE teams â€” mitigations: rehearsal runbook; cross-team dry-run 72h beforehand
5) Unexpected model quality regressions after routing opt changes â€” mitigations: holdback cohort, immediate quality-eval harness run, and canary rollback criteria
6) Capacity contention in private deployments for regulated customers â€” mitigations: reservation pinning, manual capacity checks before ramp to 60%

Capacity & traffic plan (notes):
- Dedicated pools: reserve an additional 20% headroom for D3-D10; pre-warm GPUs for predicted peak hours
- Hosted API: leverage smart routing to shift low-priority traffic to lower-cost regions during ramp windows
- Private deployments: require signoff from infra lead and customer ops at D6 before any cross-customer migration

Key metrics dashboard links (placeholders):
- latency/5xx dashboard: confluence link + grafana panel (see linked_artifacts)
- cost-per-token trend: s3://prodops-artifacts/costs/feature-activation/token-delta.csv
- eval harness reports: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/runs/1378

Owners & roles (who to call):
- Launch captain: Maya Patel (product-ops) â€” overall coordination, go/no-go
- Release engineer: Oliver Grant â€” deploy gates, rollback automation
- SRE lead: Liam Chen â€” incident triage, oncall escalation
- Perf engineer: Sofia Ramirez â€” perf validation and load test artifacts
- Customer comms: Priya Nair â€” release notes, customer status updates

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm which customer cohorts are acceptable for Canary B; get list from AMs (TODO: Priya)
- Finalize cost alert thresholds (TODO: Finance + Eng SRE)
- Validate eval harness dataset covers long conversation prompts (TODO: Research/Applied ML)
- Add explicit test scenario for function-calling and streaming edge-cases

Post-launch 72h checklist (quick):
- Confirm all KPI deltas are within thresholds for 72h window
- Run automated quality sweep on production logs against eval suite
- Collect first-week customer feedback and tag tickets PRODOPS-REQs
- Decrease ramp cooling windows if stable for 7 days and token-cost delta small

Notes on format and provenance: this is a living doc. Use it as the canonical tactical plan for the activation; copy sections into the release sprint board. I expect a couple of iterations after the dry run.

References & shorthand used:
- "KV cache" = key-value cache for autoregressive token reuse
- "smart routing" = policy-level switch between variants by latency/cost/region
- Related boards: PRODOPS-482 (link above), Release runbook in Confluence

Quick log (choppy notes):
- 2025-01-12: initial outline from Maya; merged perf numbers from Liams load test
- 2025-01-14: updated rollback criteria after SRE workshop
- 2025-01-20: QA signed off on basic feature matrix (pending long conversation tests)
